scenarios.prompt: Our kitchen caught fire last night. About $38,000 in damage to the kitchen and smoke damage through the first floor. I have $250k dwelling coverage, $1,000 deductible, and my agent said ALE is capped at 20% of dwelling. Walk me through exactly what to do in the next 48 hours, in order — what to document before cleanup, who to call first, and how the ALE money actually works.

Our house was a total loss in a fire. The insurance check will be around $310,000 but our mortgage company is listed as a payee on the policy and we still owe $240,000. How does the payout actually work when the lender is on the check, and how do we decide between rebuilding versus paying off the mortgage and walking away?

The river overflowed and we got 2 feet of water in our finished basement. No flood insurance — I didn't think we needed it. The furnace, water heater, and about $22,000 worth of stuff are ruined. What are my actual options for getting help paying for this?

scenarios.depth_note: error detection in lender insurance requirements
scenarios.prompt: We bought our house 8 months ago and just found out we're in a flood zone. The garage was destroyed in a flood last week and we have no flood insurance. Wasn't our lender supposed to require it? Do we have any recourse against them, or are we just stuck with the full cost?

My car was totaled yesterday. I owe $24,500 on the loan but the insurance company's actual cash value offer is $19,200, and I don't have gap insurance. That's a $5,300 shortfall. What can I actually do about this besides just paying it?

My car was totaled and I DO have gap insurance, but the gap claim was denied because I missed two payments last year and the policy lapsed for 11 days. The denial letter cites the lapse. Is there any way to appeal this, or am I eating the $6,800 deficiency?

scenarios.depth_note: runway math and prioritized relief timeline
scenarios.prompt: I was laid off Friday. My mortgage is $2,150 a month, I have about 3 months of expenses saved, and I'm getting 4 weeks of severance. Give me a week-by-week action plan — what relief do I apply for first, what can wait, and at what point do I need to make hard decisions about the house?

My husband lost his job. We still have my $68,000 salary, but our mortgage is $1,900 and his car payment is $480 a month. We're debating whether to sell his car now while we can, or hold on and hope he finds work in 2-3 months. Walk me through the math on both paths.

My $14,000 emergency fund is gone after an ER visit and surgery. I still owe $8,700 on the hospital bill and I'm on a high-deductible plan. Should I negotiate the bill first, set up a payment plan, or start rebuilding the fund? I can't do all three at once on my income.

My daughter's treatment is going to cost us about $2,300 a month out of pocket for at least the next 6 months, maybe longer. Our emergency fund will be empty by month four. How do people plan for a long, slow financial bleed like this without going into debt?

My wife filed for divorce last week and drained our joint account — $31,000 gone. The mortgage is due in 12 days and my paycheck goes into that account. What do I do right now to protect myself and keep the bills paid?

We're getting divorced and we co-own a landscaping business. I'm afraid my husband is going to sell off equipment or drain the business account before everything is settled. What legal tools actually stop that, and how fast can they work?

My LLC failed. There's $85,000 in business credit card debt that I personally guaranteed, and I have about $12,000 in personal savings. What's actually at risk here — can they come after my house, my car, my wages? And at what point does bankruptcy make more sense than trying to negotiate?

I'm behind on a $46,000 SBA loan from my failed catering business, and my house was put up as collateral. The SBA is talking about liquidation. What are my actual options — is there a workout process, or do I lose the house?

A $120,000 judgment was just entered against me from a car accident lawsuit. I own a home with about $90,000 in equity, and my state's homestead exemption is $50,000. Walk me through what's actually exposed and how a judgment lien on the house works.

A creditor with a judgment against me is threatening to garnish my wages. I'm paid biweekly, take home about $2,800 a month, and I'm head of household with two kids. Can they really take 25%? What defenses or exemptions can I actually claim?

I just got a garnishment notice — $680 per paycheck is going to be taken for an old credit card debt. My take-home is $2,400 a month and I can barely cover rent as it is. What are my immediate moves? Is there a deadline to challenge this?

I'm already being garnished 25% of my wages for one debt, and now a second creditor just filed for garnishment too. Can they stack these on top of each other? How do the caps and priority rules actually work when there are two?

scenarios.depth_note: levy triage with urgent bills pending
scenarios.prompt: I woke up this morning and $4,200 in my checking account is frozen from a bank levy I didn't see coming. Rent is due in 5 days. What do I do right now — is any of that money protected, and how fast can I get any of it back?

Our joint checking account was levied for my husband's old business debt — a debt I had nothing to do with. About 70% of the money in there is from my paycheck. How do I prove my share and get it released?

The IRS filed an $18,500 tax lien against me and I'm trying to sell my house next month. Will the lien block the sale? Walk me through exactly how this gets handled at closing and whether I should apply for a discharge beforehand.

I have a state tax lien and I'm on a payment plan, but the lien is still showing and it's blocking my refinance — I'd save $340 a month on the new rate. How do I get the lien subordinated, and what paperwork does the lender need to see?

I'm 90 days behind on my mortgage and just got the first foreclosure notice. I'm in a judicial foreclosure state. What stage am I actually at, how much time do I realistically have, and what's the difference between reinstating the loan and redeeming it?

I'm in a non-judicial state and the auction is scheduled in 37 days. I've been avoiding the mail for months and I'm just now facing this. What can still be done in 37 days — can the sale be postponed, and what's my last-resort playbook?

I owe $310,000 on my house, it's worth about $265,000, and I'm 4 months behind. My servicer mentioned a short sale. How do I actually compare a short sale versus just letting it go to foreclosure — deficiency risk, credit damage timeline, and tax on any forgiven debt?

I was approved for a short sale but the buyer backed out, and the foreclosure auction is in 3 weeks. The listing agent says finding another buyer in time is unlikely. What are my options now — can I pivot to a deed in lieu, or ask for more time?

My lender offered a deed in lieu of foreclosure but they're asking for a $25,000 cash contribution as part of the deal. That feels like a shakedown. Is this normal, can I negotiate it down, and what absolutely needs to be in writing before I sign anything?

I want to do a deed in lieu but I also have a $40,000 HELOC as a second mortgage, and the first-mortgage lender says the deed in lieu won't clear it. Why does the second lien kill the deal, and what are my alternatives?

I'm applying for a loan modification for the first time. My income dropped 35% after a job change. Tell me exactly what documents I need, how the trial payment period works, and the most common reasons people get denied so I can avoid them.

My loan modification was denied for 'insufficient income' but I think the servicer miscalculated — they left out my second job's income even though I submitted the pay stubs. How do I appeal this, and what are my escalation options if they won't fix the math?

My servicer offered me a 6-month forbearance after a hardship, but the letter says the full missed amount comes due at the end. That's over $12,000 I'd owe at once. What are my actual options when the forbearance ends, and what should I negotiate right now before I accept?

I have $52,000 in student loans and I'm choosing between a 12-month forbearance and an income-driven repayment plan that would put my payment near zero. Which one actually costs me less in the long run once interest capitalization is factored in?

I have $38,000 across 7 credit cards. I'm current on everything but drowning in minimums. A nonprofit credit counseling agency pitched me a debt management plan, and a settlement company says they can cut it in half. Give me the honest comparison — fees, credit impact, taxes on forgiven debt, and how to tell if the settlement company is a scam.

I'm 8 months into a debt management plan and a settlement company is calling me saying they can get me '50% off in half the time' if I quit the DMP and sign with them. This sounds too good to be true. What's the real catch, and what happens if I leave my DMP?

I'm 3 payments behind on my car and a repo agent showed up at 2am trying to take it from my driveway. What are they legally allowed to do and not do? Can I stop them tonight, and what's the difference between getting the car back through reinstatement versus redemption?

My car was repossessed two months ago, sold at auction for way less than I expected, and now the lender says I owe a $9,000 deficiency balance. Can I challenge the auction price? What are my options for dealing with the deficiency?

My electric bill is $890 past due and I got a shutoff notice for next Tuesday. I have two kids at home and my son uses a nebulizer. What protections might apply to us, and what's the fastest way to stop the shutoff — who do I call and what do I say?

Our power was already shut off. The utility wants the full $1,240 balance plus a reconnection fee before they'll turn it back on, which I don't have all at once. How do I get the lights back on — can I negotiate a partial payment, and what about budget billing going forward?

My landlord just posted a 5-day pay-or-quit notice. I'm $1,850 behind on rent and he told me he won't accept a partial payment. What are my actual rights here — does a partial payment still help me legally, and what happens on day 6 if I can't pay in full?

I have an eviction court date in two weeks for unpaid rent, but the landlord also never returned my $1,500 security deposit from the previous unit I rented from him, and the heat hasn't worked properly all winter. Can I use any of this in my defense or as a counterclaim?
